dct_description_sm: This subproject aims to 1) explore the factors and processes that (re)produce housing (in)security in the study communities of Inuvik and Yellowknife, Northwest Territories (NWT); and then, 2) examine how housing (in)security is affected in the two communities by territorial economic growth.  Housing (in)security in the NWT has long been an issue of significant concern.  Chronic shortage of housing, particularly in the smaller, more isolated communities, has been a problem for many years.  Recently, housing (in)security issues have increased in larger centres in the North, fuelled largely by an economic 'boom' underway in the territory since the late 1990s.  Among the most visible expressions of housing insecurity in the larger centres is rising homelessness.  This dataset has been developed to answer the question of how housing (in)security occurs within an overall context of unprecedented economic growth in the territory.  Plans for a major gas pipeline 'the Mackenzie Gas Project' are anticipated to proceed in the near future, which will further stimulate economic growth and drive urbanization in the two study communities: Inuvik and Yellowknife.  Further economic growth is expected to place significant pressure on an already vulnerable situation of housing (in)security and homelessness in these two centres.
